title: modadd (task-shuffled labels): no behaviour to explain
label: null result: behaviour absent as scored
behavior: 1-layer transformer, input [a, b, =], claimed to output (a + b) mod 113 at the last position. Dataset task 'modadd'.
summary: Against the labels this investigation is scored with, the model is at chance: top-1 accuracy 0.0087 on the full 113x113 grid (E0002) and 0.010 on a 200-pair sample (E0003); chance is 1/113 = 0.0088. Both pre-registered predictions of >=95% accuracy were refuted. Per protocol the investigation stopped after the baseline: there is no mechanism to explain, no algorithm was written and no verification was run. All numbers are from local-full (full precision). 3 of 40 experiments used.

# No algorithm recovered.

claims.text: On the full 113x113 grid the model's top-1 accuracy against the scored labels is 0.0087, indistinguishable from chance (1/113 = 0.0088); mean logit difference is 0.07 with std 47 (local-full).
The chance-level result is not specific to the full grid: on a 200-pair sample accuracy is 0.010 (local-full).

The labels used for scoring differ from the answers the dataset primitive displays for the same prompts: the first four prompts show answers 38, 97, 57, 103 in E0001 but are scored against 65, 41, 92, 1 in E0003.

The model is confident rather than uninformative: logit differences between the two scored labels have std 47-50 around a mean near zero, i.e. the model puts large logits on tokens that are unrelated to the scored labels.

limitations: No mechanism experiments were run: with scored labels unrelated to the model's output, every patching or ablation metric would be noise.
No verify_hypothesis run: there is no algorithm to verify.

The 8 example predictions shown by the baseline runs (0,1,2,3 in E0002; 38,97,57,103 in E0003) all equal true (a+b) mod 113. This is an observation on 8 examples, not a measured accuracy, and was not tested further because the investigation's task is defined by the scored labels.
open_questions: Does the model compute true (a+b) mod 113 at high accuracy when scored against unshuffled labels? The 8 example predictions suggest so; this needs a baseline with the unshuffled task, which is a separate investigation.
Why does the dataset primitive display answers that differ from the labels the baseline scores against?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: behaviour absent as scored

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model computes (a+b) mod 113 at the last position with high accuracy on the full grid.

prediction.statement: Top-1 accuracy on the full 113x113 grid is at least 95%

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: On a sampled dataset (n=200, seed 0), whose labels in E0001 matched true (a+b) mod 113, the model scores high accuracy; the chance result in E0002 is specific to the labels of the n=all grid.

prediction.statement: Accuracy on 200 sampled pairs is at least 95%
